A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Token Cleaning research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments across three base models and seven benchmarks, plus ablations and supplementary analyses in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original benchmark comparisons, checkpoint results, ablations, and supplementary analyses in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The influence-based scoring, token thresholding, fixed-model cleaning, and self-evolving procedure are unchanged, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 50k training pool drawn from five SFT datasets and the same seven evaluation benchmarks (Section 6.1 and Appendix D). No training or evaluation coverage changes.

E2.justification: BASE, DS2, FULL TOKENS, UNIFORM RANDOM, and RHO retain the same participation in the corresponding comparisons. The comparator sets in the reference-model and token-proportion experiments also match.

E3.justification: The model configurations, five-way data partition, evaluation metrics, token proportions, and training settings are identical in Section 6 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: Both retain the same checkpoint analyses, token-proportion and reference-model ablations, influence-score visualizations, and six illustrative token-selection examples (Section 6.3 and Appendices E–F).

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The empirical uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical entries and findings match throughout Tables 1–8, Figures 2–3, and Appendix F. For example, Table 1 retains the LLaMA-3.2-3B averages of 51.98 for fixed-model cleaning and 53.00 for self-evolving cleaning.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorem 5.1, Corollary 5.2, and Appendix C proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning the generic cleaning pipeline, self-evolving strategy, theoretical analysis, and downstream performance benefits.

C2.justification: The Matthew-effect interpretation, reference-model distribution-shift hypothesis, scale limitations, and discussion of unchanged computational speed and memory requirements are retained (Sections 5–6 and Appendices A–B).

D1.justification: Token masking, data formatting, LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, training-time estimates, and code-access information are unchanged. The code and evaluation-resource link destinations also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning relative to prior token selection and noisy-label research contain the same works and substantive discussion.

P1.justification: v3 adds equal-contribution asterisks for Jinlong Pang, Na Di, and Zhaowei Zhu, with an accompanying footnote on page 1, and updates the version stamp. Scientific prose and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The contribution markers and footnote slightly reflow the first-page author and affiliation text. Figures 1–3, Tables 1–8, and appendix example boxes retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies equal-contribution attribution on page 1. The main text and Appendices A–F retain the same methods, proofs, experimental evidence, explanations, and limitations; the limited front-matter and typesetting changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
